title: `ward secret generate`: generate passwords and secrets without revealing them
description:
From the operator, relayed by opum-agent on 2026-09-29: Ward should be able to generate passwords and secrets.

Ward's design of record has no generation surface. Spec 8's command table carries `ward secret set <alias>` with hidden input or `--stdin`, and every value in it is entered by a person; the runtime CSPRNG appears only for the vault key in 6.3. The shape this has to fit is already fixed, though: 8 says a secret command "returns metadata only", 6.2 says public inspection omits values, lengths, last-four previews and hashes, and 4.3 says a value never enters the agent session. A generated value therefore carries the same non-disclosure contract as an entered one, which is the whole point of generating it here rather than in a shell. The alias grammar, record shape and metadata surfaces come from WCLI-8, so this extends that surface instead of opening a second write path.

Scope settled, so no reader has to re-litigate it: section 5's P1 list defers "dynamic credential issuance" and "automatic provider-side rotation", and an orchestrator scope ruling of 2026-09-29 (recorded in the notes below) holds that this task is neither. Those two defer anything a provider issues or rotates remotely; this makes no remote call and involves no provider. If an implementation ever needs a provider call, that part goes back to the deferral.

Filed, not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ward secret generate <alias>` is registered in the CLI contract (help and manifest), emits the {schemaVersion, kind, data} envelope under --json, and returns the alias and the new record's metadata only; the contract test enumerates it

The generated value is stored in the vault and never reaches stdout, stderr or a log: asserted over the success path, a rejected parameter set, and a failed store; the test reads the stored bytes back out of band to prove generation and storage happened rather than asserting an absence alone

Length and character-set (or format) parameters are validated before any value is drawn; an unknown option or an out-of-range value exits 2 without echoing the supplied argument, and a rejected invocation stores nothing
No output surface carries the value, its length, a preview or a hash of it, in text or JSON, on any path; asserted with sentinel values in the T09/T11 discipline WCLI-8 already uses
The value is drawn from the runtime CSPRNG and no non-cryptographic randomness source appears in the module, checked the way scripts/check-layers.mjs checks the native binding

implementationNotes:
SCOPE RULING, recorded at opum-agent's instruction and quoted from its cross-session dispatch of 2026-09-29 (orchestrator design decision, not this session's): local generation is IN scope and is NOT the section 5 P1-deferred "dynamic credential issuance" or "automatic provider-side rotation". Those two defer anything a provider issues or rotates remotely. This task makes no remote call and involves no provider, and it produces a value that then carries exactly the non-disclosure contract of an entered one. If an implementation ever needs a provider call, that part goes back to the deferral.

Why it is on the record rather than left in the dispatch: the boundary was named in this task's description when it was filed, as a question for whoever owns it, and this is the answer to it. A reader who finds the description alone should not have to reconstruct that the question was settled.
